title: Runtime permissions, and the flow when the user says no twice

videos.script: Most permissions your app holds were never asked for. One kind is, while the app runs, in a dialog the system draws. {{model}} And the system remembers. Say no once, and the app may explain and ask again. Say no twice, and the dialog stops appearing. Only the settings screen can change it then. {{asking}} So you ask from a composable, at the moment the student wants the thing. A launcher, an answer, and a note to yourself that you asked. {{decision}} Then one plain function turns four answers into one decision. Never asked, refused once, refused twice, or nothing to ask. {{card}} The card says something different in each case. A benefit, then an honest promise, then where the switch is. {{twice}} Then a test plays the system's part, refuses twice, and watches the card change. {{phone}} And last, what only a phone shows: the dialog itself, and the permissions that grant less than they seem.
